title: Experimental Evaluation of Passive Polarization Compensation Techniques for Fiber-Distributed Polarization-Entangled Photons
authors: Gayatri Thik, Amit Loyal, Srinivasan K, Raghavan G
abstract: Entanglement distribution through optical fibers is essential for quantum communication networks; however, fiber transmission can alter photon polarization and modify the observed correlations of polarization-entangled states, necessitating polarization compensation to recover the desired entangled state in the measurement basis. Here, we experimentally evaluate two passive polarization compensation techniques: a free-space Quarter-Half-Quarter (QHQ) waveplate configuration and an in-fiber three-paddle Fiber Polarization Controller (FPC). The polarization transformation along each downconverted-photon path is independently compensated through a systematic path-by-path optimization procedure. Using both techniques, we recover high-quality polarization correlations and entanglement, with visibilities exceeding $93\%$ in three mutually unbiased bases and fidelities above $94.5\%$. The results demonstrate comparable restoration using free-space waveplate-based and fiber-based control, establishing a systematic framework for laboratory and short-reach quantum communication links.
summary: This paper experimentally evaluates two passive methods—free-space waveplates and fiber polarization controllers—to compensate for polarization degradation in entangled photons traveling through optical fibers. By optimizing each path independently, the authors successfully restored high-quality entanglement, demonstrating that both free-space and fiber-based control methods are equally effective for short-reach quantum links.
main_problem: Fiber transmission degrades the polarization correlations of entangled photons, necessitating polarization compensation to restore the desired entangled state for quantum communication.
main_result: Both free-space (QHQ) and fiber-based (FPC) passive compensation techniques successfully restore high-quality polarization correlations and entanglement, achieving fidelities above 94.5%.
method: The authors experimentally evaluated two passive compensation methods—QHQ waveplates and FPC—using an independent, path-by-path optimization procedure on the signal and idler paths.
model_or_system: The system involves distributing polarization-entangled photons through single-mode optical fibers. The polarization transformation is modeled as a unitary operation, and compensation aims to apply the inverse unitary transformation.
key_observables: Polarization correlations, Bell–CHSH parameter, Visibility (exceeding 93%), and State Fidelity (above 94.5%).
important_parameters: The comparison is between QHQ (free-space) and FPC (fiber-based) compensation methods for short-reach links.
main_assumptions: The compensation is implemented using passive elements, and the optimization procedure is performed path-by-path before final state characterization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setups for both QHQ and FPC compensation, and show the measured polarization correlations and reconstructed two-qubit density matrices before and after compensation.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of fiber-induced polarization degradation, then details the two compensation methods (QHQ and FPC), describes the systematic path-by-path optimization procedure, and finally presents quantitative comparisons of the recovered entanglement quality.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental validation of systematic, passive compensation techniques necessary for building reliable quantum communication links over optical fibers, directly impacting photonic quantum information networks.
